references.name:
Adam Smith,
      The Wealth of Nations
references.desc:
Central subject of Chapter III; foundation of all
      subsequent economic thought

references.name:
Karl Marx,
      Das Kapital
references.desc:
Central subject of Chapter VI; labor theory of value,
      surplus value, falling rate of profit

references.name:
John Maynard Keynes,
      The General Theory
references.desc:
Central subject of Chapter IX; savings-investment
      split, multiplier, involuntary unemployment

references.name:
Karl Polanyi,
      The Great Transformation
references.desc:
Recommended for the social history of the market
      revolution; Heilbroner calls it "wholly absorbing"

references.name:
R.H. Tawney,
      Religion and the Rise of Capitalism
references.desc:
"A class by itself, a profound work in an
      unsurpassable style"

references.name:
Max Weber,
      The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism
references.desc:
The religious roots of capitalist acquisitiveness;
      more demanding but classic

references.name:
Joseph Schumpeter,
      History of Economic Analysis
references.desc: "Masterpiece, as brilliant and opinionated as its author"

references.name:
Edmund Wilson,
      To the Finland Station
references.desc: Best entry point for Marx; "like reading a novel"

references.name:
Matthew Josephson,
      The Robber Barons
references.desc:
"Trenchantly and rollickingly illustrated" account of
      Gilded Age capitalists; context for Veblen

references.name:
Lord Robert Skidelsky,
      John Maynard Keynes
references.desc: "Brilliant" biography; recommended for full Keynes portrait

references.name:
Friedrich Hayek,
      The Road to Serfdom
references.desc:
Keynes read it, sympathized with the concern,
      disagreed with the conclusions — wanted more planning,
      not less, in responsible hands

references.name:
J.A. Hobson,
      Imperialism
Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
references.desc:
Marx's dialectical method is a materialist inversion
      of Hegel's dialectic of ideas

references.name: Jeremy Bentham
references.desc:
Felicific Calculus — pleasure and pain as the
      only true human motivators; foundation of
      Edgeworth's mathematical psychics

references.name:
François Quesnay,
      Tableau Économique
references.desc:
Physiocracy — the first systematic model of
      economic circulation; Smith's predecessor in Paris
